title: daysBetween/hoursBetween — the only functions that derive the classifier's numeric inputs from Dates — have zero assertions
trigger_condition: The threshold matrix is tested only through pre-computed integers; the Date→number derivation that production actually uses is untested, so an inverted argument order or a changed divisor shifts every threshold silently.
guard_snippet: Absent: no assertion such as `expect(hoursBetween(chargeDate, NOW)).toBe(72)` / `expect(daysBetween(lastLoginAt, NOW)).toBe(14)`, and none covering the `Math.floor` boundary (72.9h → 72, 14.9d → 14) that decides exactly-at-threshold classifications.
potential_consequence: `daysBetween(chargeDate, now)` at packages/api/src/routers/refund.ts:116 and `hoursBetween(profile.lastLoginAt, now)` at :124 are the sole producers of `daysSinceCharge` and `hoursSinceLastSuccessfulLogin`. Swapping to `daysBetween(now, chargeDate)` — which is `Math.floor` of a negative number — flips both to large negative values, which satisfy `<= 7` and `>= 72` simultaneously, so every refund request auto-approves regardless of evidence. All 23 classifier tests stay green because every one of them supplies `daysSinceCharge`/`hoursSinceLastSuccessfulLogin` as literals.
consumer: `buildClassifierInput` in packages/api/src/routers/refund.ts:116 and :124, whose output is passed straight into `classifyRefundRequest` at :163
evidence: Repo-wide grep for `\b(daysBetween|hoursBetween)\b` across all *.ts/*.tsx outside node_modules returned exactly five hits: the two definitions (packages/api/src/lib/refund-classifier.ts:135, :139), the two imports (packages/api/src/routers/refund.ts:19, :20) and the two call sites (:116, :124). No test file appears. Read packages/api/src/lib/__tests__/refund-classifier.test.ts in full (252 lines): the `input()` factory at :19-29 hard-codes `daysSinceCharge: 3` and `hoursSinceLastSuccessfulLogin: 1` as numbers, and no test in the file constructs a `Date` or calls either helper. Confirmed the helper bodies are `Math.floor((to.getTime() - from.getTime()) / DAY_MS)` and `/ HOUR_MS`.
